To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) decoupled hyperparameter optimization for mask discovery and mask evaluation can lead to substantially higher performance, 2) the decoupled hyperparameters for mask evaluation should be chosen to match the hyperparameters used for final evaluation, and 3) this effect is causally mediated through layerwise pruning ratios, which should be chosen to maximize the final performance

the best hyperparameter configuration for training a model is not necessarily the best configuration for pruning and that different hyperparameter values for mask discovery yield masks with materially distinct layerwise pruning ratios, and that the decouple find-eval phenomenon can be causally mediated by the layerwise pruning ratios.
We demonstrate that the best hyperparameters to discover a mask are not the same as those to evaluate the mask.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our work demonstrates that decoupling hyperparameter selection for model pruning can lead to better masks, which in turn lead to better performance.
we have shown that decoupled find- eval hyperparameters lead to masks with higher eventual performance.
we show that there is an optimal hyperparameter configuration for finding a mask that is different from the hyperparameter configuration for evaluating a mask.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in general, it is better to use the best H_eval for finding the mask, rather than the best H_eval overall.

we found the "find" and "eval" hyperparameters are not necessarily the same, and we can find better masks using the "find" hyperparameters that are different from the "eval" ones, and we can get a better model using those masks.
we decoupled hyperparameters for model pruning, and we found that the best hyperparameters for model evaluation are not the best for model pruning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for magnitude pruning, the hyperparameters used to discover a mask are more impactful than the hyperparameters used in the evaluation stage.

the training configuration which yields the best model performance may not yield the best mask, and that decoupling the hyperparameters for finding and evaluating the mask can lead to substantial performance gains.
we should not blindly trust the results of pruning without testing whether a different hyperparameter configuration for mask discovery could have led to higher performance.
